title: Invert Binary Tree
statement: You get the root of a binary tree. Mirror it: every node swaps its left and right child, all the way down. Return the root of the mirrored tree. The tree can be empty.

example.caption: Every node swapped its two sides, so the picture is a mirror image.

idea.sentence: A mirror image is just every node swapping its two children, so solve each child first and then swap at this node.

jargon.plain: A function that calls itself on a smaller piece. For a tree, the smaller pieces are the left and right subtrees.
A node together with everything hanging below it. It is a small tree of its own.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the tree as a level-order array, null for a missing child, e.g. [4,2,7,1,3]

compare.bruteLabel: Build a second, mirrored copy of the tree
compare.optimalLabel: Swap in place (stack depth is the height)
compare.unit: extra memory cells, for a balanced tree

rows.name: Build a mirrored copy
rows.note: Allocates a whole new tree just to throw the old one away.

rows.name: Swap in place, recursive
rows.note: Each node is touched once. The only extra memory is the call stack.

fast.takeaway: You must visit every node once, so O(n) time is the floor. Swapping in place keeps the extra memory down to the height of the tree.

stages.title: Empty spot
stages.note: A missing child has nothing to flip. Return null and let the parent carry on.

stages.title: Flip both sides first
stages.note: Call the function on the right child and on the left child. Each call returns a finished, mirrored subtree.

stages.title: Swap and return
stages.note: Put the flipped right subtree on the left and the flipped left subtree on the right. Return this node.

edges.title: Empty tree
edges.why: The root is null, so the very first check returns null.

edges.title: Single node
edges.why: Both children are empty. Swapping two nulls changes nothing.

edges.title: Only one child
edges.why: The swap still happens. A real child trades places with an empty slot.

edges.title: Long chain
edges.why: The whole chain leans the other way. Recursion goes as deep as the tree is tall.

gotchas.text: Swap even when one child is missing. Skipping the swap for a node with one child leaves it leaning the wrong way.
Do not write root.left = root.right and then root.right = root.left. The second line reads the value you just overwrote. Use temporaries, or recurse first as here.
Children are TreeNode | null. Test with if (!root), and never with root === undefined, because a missing child is null.
Touching root.Left when root is nil panics. The nil check must come before any field access.
root.Left, root.Right = left, right is a safe parallel assignment, so Go needs no temporary for a plain swap.

recap.pattern: Tree recursion: act after the children
recap.key: Mirror each subtree, then swap the two sides at this node. Return the node.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(h) call stack.
moves: Recurse into the right child and the left child
Assign them crosswise: left gets the flipped right
